decks.title: Your website: a guided tour
decks.desc: Who Lee-Elle is, the thinking behind each of the five designs and why it suits her, Hebrew in every design, and what we can do.

slides.h: Your website
slides.sub: Private Hebrew Tuition with Lee-Elle Horowitz
slides.note: Five designs, in English and in Hebrew. A draft, 25 November 2026.

slides.h: One person, and one minute on a phone

left.title: Who Lee-Elle is, in her words
points: South African-born and Israel-raised, a fluent Hebrew speaker who later moved to the UK
Teaches Hebrew to children, teenagers and adults, in London and on Zoom
Experience with children aged 7 to 11; Enhanced DBS checked
First Class Honours BA, Guildford School of Acting: an actor-musician who also teaches singing, trombone and guitar

right.title: What the site has to do
points: A parent arrives on a phone, usually from a recommendation, and decides in about a minute
They look for: who teaches, what ages, where, whether it is safe
So every design puts her photo, the lessons and the facts on the first screen, and one action: ask about lessons

slides.h: Five ideas, each taken from her own life
slides.intro: Not five colour schemes on one layout: each design starts from a different part of who she is and how she teaches, and speaks to a different parent.
rows: Alef-bet

slides.h: Her photo, seen through the first letter
why: Hebrew starts with alef. She teaches complete beginners and reading and writing, so the page is built from the alphabet.
Her photo inside the alef says, before a word is read: this is the teacher who opens the language.
All 22 letters arrive across the page, right to left; every section opens on its own letter, with its English name.
slides.sees: A parent of a young beginner sees a teacher and the letters their child will learn.

slides.h: The page is a conversation, like her lessons
why: Her approach is conversation: "building confidence, developing conversational skills".
So there is no headline, only a chat: a parent's first question, her reply typing in, her photo beside it.
The facts are quick replies (ages, London, Zoom, DBS), and the button is the reply box.
slides.sees: A parent with questions gets them answered in the order they would ask.

slides.h: was → is → will be
why: She teaches past, present and future tenses, so the page is organised by them.
Past is her story, in sepia: South Africa, Israel, the UK, Guildford. Present is lessons today, in colour. Future is an empty frame marked "you".
The headline is grammar itself; the page ends on the student's goal and the button.
slides.sees: A parent sees where their child would start, and where lessons lead.

slides.h: A theatre programme, from her training
why: She trained as an actor-musician at the Guildford School of Acting, with a First Class Honours BA.
The page is a playbill: her name like a poster, her photo under a spotlight, curtains that open once.
Hebrew is the main act; music and audition preparation are act two; a ticket stub asks about lessons.
slides.sees: A teenager who sings or acts, or their parent, sees a teacher who has been on stage.

slides.h: An exercise book: just the facts
why: She supports Hebrew at school and in supplementary Jewish education, so the page is a school exercise book.
The cover is filled in (Name, Subject: Hebrew, Also: Music) with her photo taped on; the lessons are ticked in red pen.
One plain column, which prints cleanly.
slides.sees: A parent who wants facts, not effects, gets them on one page to print.

slides.h: עברית, in every single design
slides.p: Not a translation pasted on: each of the five designs is rebuilt right to left, with Hebrew type, the layout mirrored, and the letters used as material. One switch at the top of every page changes the language, and the same design stays on screen.
points: Ten pages from one set of words: five designs, two languages
For Hebrew-speaking parents in the UK, and for children growing up between two languages
The translation is marked on every page as not yet checked by her, until she has corrected it

slides.h: Five different first screens, on a phone
slides.p: Most parents arrive on a phone, so each design is made phone first, with her photo, the lessons and one button on the very first screen. Every page passes accessibility checks in light and dark mode.

slides.h: A sovereign website, made for one person
items: Five designs, each from a different part of her life, all from the words she supplied
Every design in English and Hebrew, right to left, with a switch on every page
All content in JSON files; the pages are built from them, so a change is made once
Status, tasks, photos and credits, quality checks and every change, at /admin/
Links, accessibility in light and dark, phone and desktop, every time
No server, no cookies, no tracking; plain files she owns and can move anywhere

slides.h: What we need from you
points: Which design you like best, or which parts of which.
Corrections to the Hebrew, and your name in Hebrew if you want it.
Your own photos, with the photographer's name for each.
Which contact details, if any, visitors should see; prices and availability only if you want them shown.
Your approval, when you are happy.

slides.h: Plain files, in a place you own
slides.p: No server, no cookies, no tracking. The files, the history and the address can move anywhere, at any time.

decks.title: Behind the scenes: how this site was made
decks.desc: The agents, the pipeline, content in JSON, the checks, the design rounds and what makes the site sovereign.

slides.h: How this site was made
slides.note: Built on 25 November 2026 by a team of AI agents working for Dinis Cruz

slides.h: One request, a team of agents, each with one job
slides.intro: Each agent does one job and keeps its notes in public, so its thinking stays sharp and anyone can see who did what.
steps: Takes the request, checks it is complete, starts a dedicated keeper. Never builds.
Makes the repository, the address and its certificate.
Writes the design brief: five ideas, not colour skins.
b.site.lee-elle-horowitz builds and keeps the site, in its own session.
Reviews each round with synthetic personas, including an Israeli-born parent reading the Hebrew.
Lists the site in the hub once she approves it.

slides.h: From request to live site
steps: filed in the Sovereign Website factory
seeded with checks and a deploy workflow
the keeper signs every commit with its own key
a push to dev publishes in a minute or two

slides.h: Five ideas, then rounds with synthetic parents
slides.intro: design.b.rounds puts each version in front of synthetic personas and asks one question: would you book a Hebrew lesson for your child here?
rounds: Five designs, each from its own idea
Hebrew letters in every design; the facts parents look for higher up
The alphabet right to left; no empty placeholders; one voice, hers
Each design opens differently, with her photo on the first screen
Conversation and Notebook rise to 3 of 5; phone fixes

slides.h: Every word lives in JSON
points: site/data/content/en.json: her words, as she supplied them.
site/data/content/he.json: the Hebrew translation, for her to check.
site.json, start.json, tour.json and admin.json: everything else.
tools/designs/build.py turns them into plain HTML pages, in both languages. It holds no words of its own.
slides.code: en.json + he.json  →  build.py  →  10 design pages, 2 home pages, 2 pickers, the tour and the admin area

slides.h: Right to left, properly
slides.p: The Hebrew pages are not a mirror image of the English ones: the html element is marked lang="he" dir="rtl", the CSS uses start and end instead of left and right, English names inside Hebrew sit in their own direction, and Hebrew type is set heavier and larger.
points: One stylesheet per design, plus one that turns any of them right to left
A switch at the top of every page, and a button that appears as you scroll
Checked by a Hebrew-speaking persona in every round

slides.h: Checked before every push
points: Build, link previews and internal links.
HTML validity, and accessibility (axe) on every page, at desktop and phone width, in light and in dark mode.
No em dashes, a leak scan for secrets.
No page longer than 8,000 px on a phone, and no sideways scrolling.
Nothing loaded from another website: no fonts, scripts or trackers.

slides.h: Signed, and public
points: Each agent makes its own signing key; only the public half is published.
Every commit is signed and carries the agent's name and session.
The keeper's notes, open work and decisions are in the repository, for anyone to read.

slides.h: A website its owner controls
slides.p: Static files in one repository: no server code, no cookies, no tracking. It belongs to Lee-Elle, and can move anywhere.
